updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.title: Move Cmdr to your Applications folder

@updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.title.description: Title of the dialog shown when a new version is available but Cmdr is running from somewhere it can't update itself. Sentence case. "Applications" is the macOS folder name, which Apple localizes per system language.
@updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.title.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.translo: A new version is ready, but macOS is running Cmdr from a temporary read-only copy of itself. That''s what happens when you open an app straight from where you downloaded it, and it means updates have nowhere to land.

@updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.transl.description: First paragraph of the move-to-Applications dialog, for the macOS App Translocation case (the app was opened from the Downloads folder). Explains why the update can't be applied. Conversational.
@updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.transl.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.readOnl: A new version is ready, but Cmdr is running from a read-only spot, usually a disk image that''s still mounted. That means updates have nowhere to land.

@updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.readOn.description: First paragraph of the move-to-Applications dialog, for the case where the app runs from a read-only volume such as a mounted .dmg disk image. Conversational.
@updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.readOn.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.howTo: Quit Cmdr, drag it into your Applications folder, and open it from there. Every update after that arrives on its own.

@updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.howTo.description: Second paragraph of the move-to-Applications dialog: the instruction the user should follow. "Applications" is the macOS folder name, which Apple localizes per system language.
@updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.howTo.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

@updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.gotIt.description: The only button in the move-to-Applications dialog; closes it. Short, friendly acknowledgement.
@updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.gotIt.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.
